title: Raj Ghat Delhi - Mahatma Gandhi Memorial & Travel Guide
content:
Raj Ghat - Delhi

Raj Ghat in Delhi is a simple yet powerful memorial dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation. Surrounded by lush green lawns, shady trees, and quiet pathways, it offers a peaceful atmosphere where visitors from India and abroad come to pay tribute.

Raj Ghat marks the cremation site of Mahatma Gandhi after his assassination on 31 January 1948. At the center lies a black marble platform, inscribed with Gandhi’s last words “Hey Ram.” An eternal flame burns beside it, symbolizing the timeless legacy of truth and non-violence that Gandhi stood for.

Walking around Raj Ghat feels like stepping into a space of silence and reflection. The beautifully maintained gardens, open walkways, and calm environment encourage visitors to pause and think about Gandhi’s life and teachings. Just nearby, there are also memorials of other important leaders of India, such as Jawaharlal Nehru, Lal Bahadur Shastri, Indira Gandhi, and Atal Bihari Vajpayee, making the area an important national heritage site.

For travelers, Raj Ghat is not only a place of history but also a quiet break from the rush of Delhi. Entry is free of charge, and it remains open daily from 6:30 AM to 6:00 PM. The best time to visit is between October and March, when the weather is pleasant. Early mornings are especially serene, offering the most peaceful experience.

Located on Ring Road, near the banks of the Yamuna River, Raj Ghat is also close to other landmarks like the Red Fort and Shakti Sthal, making it easy to add to a day of sightseeing in Delhi.

For anyone visiting the capital, Raj Ghat is more than just a tourist attraction. It is a place of respect, reflection, and remembrance—where the simplicity of the memorial reflects the greatness of the man it honors.

Best Time to Visit: October to March for pleasant weather. Early mornings or late afternoons are best for quiet moments and soft natural light.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: Nearest station is Delhi Gate (Violet Line) or Indraprastha (Blue Line), both a short rickshaw ride away.
  • By Bus/Auto: Well-connected by DTC buses and autos from central and Old Delhi.
  • By Car: Limited parking available near the entrance.

Entry Fee: 

No Fee,  It is Free for all visitors.

Travel Tip: Bring a hat or umbrella if visiting midday—though the lawns are shady, the walkways can get sunny.
